name: CI

# NOTE: This workflow builds/tests with dummy env vars.
# It catches compile errors, unit-test failures, and type regressions.
# It does NOT exercise the real Vercel runtime or real backend services.
#
# For PRs targeting main, a SEPARATE required check runs:
#   .github/workflows/preview-smoke.yml  — "Smoke test Vercel preview"
# That workflow waits for the Vercel preview deployment and hits
# /api/health + homepage against real env vars, catching runtime failures
# that dummy-key builds cannot detect (see incident: Next.js 16.2.1).
# The health probe fails on non-200 or JSON status != "healthy".
#
# DO-H1: Direct `develop` pushes do NOT get an equivalent runtime smoke
# check. `vercel.json`'s ignoreCommand skips the Vercel build for every
# non-production deploy with no PR id — i.e. every direct `develop` push —
# so no preview deployment is ever created for these commits. A prior
# develop-push smoke job (DO-M5) waited up to 5 minutes for a preview that
# could never appear, then reported SUCCESS via its timeout branch without
# having probed anything. It was removed rather than fixed to fail-on-
# timeout, since deleting it also reclaims the ~5.3 min of runner time it
# burned on every push for zero signal. Runtime regressions on `develop`
# commits are now only caught when a PR from `develop` to `main` runs
# `preview-smoke.yml` ("Smoke test Vercel preview"), which has a real
# preview to probe. See docs/operations/alerting-runbook.md.

on:
  # Callable app work is isolated and never grants production authority.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      source_sha:
        description: Exact admitted app checkout, distinct from caller definition.
        required: true
        type: string
      profile:
        description: Isolated full or nightly app work.
        required: true
        type: string
      invocation_id:
        description: Unique caller job ID, safe ASCII and at most 64 characters.
        required: true
        type: string
  push:
    branches: [develop, main]
    # DO-M7 (#834): skip the full lint/test/build suite for commits that
    # touch only prose. Filters the `push` trigger ONLY — `pull_request`
    # below stays unfiltered because "Lint & Typecheck", "Test", and
    # "Build" are required status checks for the `main` branch protection
    # rule. Filtering pull_request too could leave a docs-only release PR
    # waiting forever on a required context that never runs. See
    # e2e.yml/lighthouse.yml for the same convention.
    paths-ignore:
      - "docs/**"
      - "README.md"
      - "CHANGELOG.md"
      - "ROADMAP.md"
      - "AGENTS.md"
  pull_request:
    branches: [develop, main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ inputs.profile == '' && inputs.source_sha == '' && inputs.invocation_id == '' && (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'pull_request') && github.workflow_ref == format('juan294/paisaxe/.github/workflows/ci.yml@{0}', github.ref) && format('{0}-{1}', github.workflow, github.ref) || format('paisaxe-ci-full-call-{0}-{1}-{2}', github.run_id, github.run_attempt, inputs.invocation_id) }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ inputs.profile == '' && inputs.source_sha == '' && inputs.invocation_id == '' && (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'pull_request') && github.workflow_ref == format('juan294/paisaxe/.github/workflows/ci.yml@{0}', github.ref) && github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:

      inputs.profile == '' && inputs.source_sha == '' && inputs.invocation_id == '' && (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'pull_request') && github.workflow_ref == format('juan294/paisaxe/.github/workflows/ci.yml@{0}', github.ref) && (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop')

      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      checks: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/validate-merged-pr.yml
    with:
      required_checks: '["Lint & Typecheck","Test","Build"]'

          ENV: ''
          LD_PRELOAD: ''
          LD_LIBRARY_PATH: ''
          LD_AUDIT: ''
          LD_ORIGIN_PATH: ''
          DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES: ''
          DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH: ''
          PYTHONPATH: ''
          PYTHONHOME: ''
          PYTHONSTARTUP: ''

          import os,re,stat,subprocess,hashlib
          from pathlib import Path

          expected=os.environ.get('SOURCE_SHA','')

          env={'PATH':'/usr/bin:/bin','GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM':'1','GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL':'/dev/null','GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS':'1','GIT_GRAFT_FILE':'/dev/null'}

           return subprocess.check_output(['/usr/bin/git','--no-replace-objects','--git-dir='+str(metadata),'--work-tree='+str(root),'-c','core.useReplaceRefs=false','-c','core.hooksPath=/dev/null','-c','core.fsmonitor=false','-c','core.ignoreCase=false','-c','core.attributesFile=/dev/null',*args],cwd=root,env=env,timeout=10)

           assert name and not name.startswith(b'/') and all(part not in (b'',b'.',b'..',b'.git') for part in name.split(b'/'))
           committed[name]=(mode,oid)
          index={}

           if not entry:continue
           fields,name=entry.split(b'\t',1);mode,oid,stage=fields.split()
           assert stage==b'0' and name not in index
           index[name]=(mode,oid)
          assert committed==index
          for entry in git('ls-files','-v','-z').split(b'\0'):
           if entry:assert entry[:2]==b'H '
          assert not git('ls-files','--others','--exclude-standard','-z')
          for name,(mode,oid) in committed.items():
           path=root/os.fsdecode(name)
           parent=path.parent
           while parent!=root:
            assert parent.is_dir() and not parent.is_symlink();parent=parent.parent
           before=path.lstat()
           if mode==b'120000':
            assert stat.S_ISLNK(before.st_mode);data=os.fsencode(os.readlink(path))
           else:
            assert stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode) and before.st_nlink==1 and bool(before.st_mode&0o111)==(mode==b'100755') and before.st_size<=134217728
            with open(path,'rb') as source:data=source.read(134217729)
            assert len(data)==before.st_size
           after=path.lstat()
           assert (before.st_dev,before.st_ino,before.st_mode,before.st_size,before.st_mtime_ns)==(after.st_dev,after.st_ino,after.st_mode,after.st_size,after.st_mtime_ns)
           assert hashlib.sha1(b'blob '+str(len(data)).encode()+b'\0'+data).hexdigest().encode()==oid
          assert git('rev-parse','--verify','HEAD').strip().decode()==expected
          PY

        uses: actions/setup-node@v7

name: E2E Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [develop, main]
    # DO-M7 (#834): broadened from docs/research|plans|agents/** to the
    # whole docs/** tree plus root prose files — a docs-only commit outside
    # those three subfolders (e.g. docs/operations/**, docs/project/**)
    # was still triggering the full E2E + Visual Regression suite. Filters
    # `push` only; `pull_request` stays unfiltered because "Playwright E2E"
    # is a required status check for the `main` branch protection rule —
    # filtering it there could leave a docs-only release PR waiting forever
    # on a required context that never runs.
    paths-ignore:
      - "docs/**"
      - "README.md"
      - "CHANGELOG.md"
      - "ROADMAP.md"
      - "AGENTS.md"
  pull_request:
    branches: [develop, main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  develop_push_source:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      checks: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/validate-merged-pr.yml
    with:
      required_checks: '["Playwright E2E","Visual Regression"]'

  e2e:
    name: Playwright E2E
    needs: develop_push_source
    if: always() && needs.develop_push_source.outputs.validated_by_pr != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    env:
      PLAYWRIGHT_CHROME_CHANNEL: chrome
      SECRETS_WITHHELD_PR: >-
        ${{
          github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
          (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork == true ||
           github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')
        }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Check authenticated QA secrets
        if: env.SECRETS_WITHHELD_PR != 'true'
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL }}
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: ${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY }}
          SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY }}
          QA_TEST_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.QA_TEST_USER_EMAIL }}
          QA_TEST_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.QA_TEST_USER_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          for key in \
            NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL \
            NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY \
            SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY \
            QA_TEST_USER_EMAIL \
            QA_TEST_USER_PASSWORD; do
            if [ -z "${!key}" ]; then
              echo "Missing required secret: ${key}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done

      - name: Install canvas system dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/install-canvas-deps

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install Playwright system dependencies
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: npx playwright install-deps chromium

      - name: Verify system Chrome
        run: google-chrome --version

      - name: Build application
        run: npm run build
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_build
          VOYAGE_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_build
          # Keep the browser bundle deterministic: immersive E2E tests mock
          # /api/feature-flags per scenario. A live URL here server-seeds the
          # production flags at build time and bypasses those browser mocks.
          # The real public credentials remain available to the runtime step
          # below, where the authenticated QA fixture signs in.
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: https://example.supabase.co
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: dummy_key_for_build

      - name: Run E2E tests with authenticated journey
        if: env.SECRETS_WITHHELD_PR != 'true'
        run: npm run test:e2e
        env:
          CI: true
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_e2e
          VOYAGE_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_e2e
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL }}
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: ${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY }}
          SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY }}
          MAINTENANCE_MODE: "false"
          STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: sk_test_dummy_for_e2e
          STRIPE_DAY_PASS_PRICE_ID: price_test_dummy_for_e2e
          QA_TEST_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.QA_TEST_USER_EMAIL }}
          QA_TEST_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.QA_TEST_USER_PASSWORD }}

      # GitHub withholds Actions secrets from Dependabot and fork PRs. Run the
      # deterministic anonymous suite with dummy Supabase values in that trust
      # context. Authenticated coverage remains mandatory for ordinary PRs and
      # branch pushes, and every dependency update receives it again after the
      # vetted change is integrated onto develop.
      - name: Run E2E tests without secret-backed authenticated journey
        if: env.SECRETS_WITHHELD_PR == 'true'
        run: >-
          npm run test:e2e --
          --grep-invert="QA Journey: Authenticated User"
        env:
          CI: true
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_e2e
          VOYAGE_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_e2e
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: https://example.supabase.co
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: dummy_key_for_e2e
          MAINTENANCE_MODE: "false"
          STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: sk_test_dummy_for_e2e
          STRIPE_DAY_PASS_PRICE_ID: price_test_dummy_for_e2e

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install Playwright Chromium

      - name: Build application
        run: npm run build
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_build
          VOYAGE_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_build
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: https://example.supabase.co
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: dummy_key_for_build

      - name: Run visual regression tests
        run: npm run test:e2e:visual
        env:
          CI: true
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_e2e
          VOYAGE_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_e2e
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: https://example.supabase.co

      - name: Upload visual diff artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        with:

      # Argument: preset, Given: mobile, Choices: perf, experimental, desktop").
      # Omitting the key falls back to Lighthouse's default settings, whose
      # formFactor is already "mobile" (see lighthouse/core/config/constants.js);
      # the desktop config file is the one that opts OUT of that default.
      #
      # BUDGET NOTE: lighthouserc.mobile.json sets largest-contentful-paint to
      # 5500ms, not the 4000ms desktop budget it was originally copied from.
      # That 4000ms was never calibrated for mobile and the gate failed on all
      # three runs it ever had (median-run LCP 4063.9 / 4445.1 / 4551.0ms —
      # a ~490ms spread on a shared runner). Mobile emulation applies 4x CPU
      # throttling and slow-4G network on top of a deliberately inflated
      # 25-story fallback fixture, so it is a strictly harsher bar than the
      # desktop preset. 5500ms sits ~950ms above the worst observed run: wide
      # enough to absorb runner noise, tight enough to still catch a real
      # regression. Getting /immersive under 4000ms on mobile is tracked
      # separately as real perf work in issue #926.
      #
      # categories:performance is likewise 0.6 on mobile, not the desktop 0.7.
      # Observed mobile scores run 0.64-0.70+ (one run passed 0.7, the next gave
      # 0.64/0.69/0.69), so the desktop-derived 0.7 sits inside the run-to-run
      # noise band and the gate was roughly a coin flip. 0.6 is below the
      # observed floor: it no longer flakes, but a genuine regression (a drop to
      # ~0.5) still hard-fails. Raising it back to 0.7 is part of #926.
      # total-blocking-time is deliberately left at warn/500ms (observed
      # 696-767ms) so the regression stays visible instead of being tuned away.
      - name: Run Lighthouse CI (mobile)
        uses: treosh/lighthouse-ci-action@v12
        with:
          configPath: './lighthouserc.mobile.json'
          uploadArtifacts: true
          artifactName: lighthouse-results-mobile
        env:
          # Dummy values for server runtime (APIs not called during audit)
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_build
          VOYAGE_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_build
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: https://example.supabase.co
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: dummy_key_for_build
          MAINTENANCE_MODE: "false"

name: Bundle Size Analysis

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [develop, main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  analyze:
    name: Analyze Bundle Size
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20

    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build
        env:
          # Dummy values for build (APIs not called during build)
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_build
          VOYAGE_API_KEY: dummy_key_for_build
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: https://example.supabase.co
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: dummy_key_for_build

      - name: Analyze bundle
        id: bundle
        run: |
          echo "## Bundle Size Report" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| Directory | Size |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "|-----------|------|" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          if [ -d ".next/static" ]; then
            STATIC_SIZE=$(du -sh .next/static | cut -f1)
            echo "| \`.next/static\` | $STATIC_SIZE |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

          if [ -d ".next/server" ]; then
            SERVER_SIZE=$(du -sh .next/server | cut -f1)
            echo "| \`.next/server\` | $SERVER_SIZE |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

          TOTAL_SIZE=$(du -sh .next | cut -f1)
          echo "| **Total \`.next\`** | **$TOTAL_SIZE** |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          echo "### Largest JS bundles" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo '```' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          find .next -name "*.js" -type f -exec du -h {} + | sort -rh | head -20 >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo '```' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          # Save values for PR comment
          echo "static_size=${STATIC_SIZE:-N/A}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "server_size=${SERVER_SIZE:-N/A}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "total_size=${TOTAL_SIZE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # PE-H3: du -sh above is informational only and can never fail. This step is the
      # actual hard gate — it sums real gzip bytes per route from the Turbopack output
      # (the bundler that ships to production) and fails the job if any route exceeds
      # its committed budget in scripts/check-bundle-budget.ts.
      - name: Enforce per-route bundle budget
        id: budget
        run: npm run check-bundle-budget

      - name: Comment on PR
        if: always()
        uses: actions/github-script@v9
        with:
          script: |
            const staticSize = '${{ steps.bundle.outputs.static_size }}';
            const serverSize = '${{ steps.bundle.outputs.server_size }}';
            const totalSize = '${{ steps.bundle.outputs.total_size }}';
            const budgetOutcome = '${{ steps.budget.outcome }}' === 'success' ? '✅ within budget' : '❌ budget exceeded — see job logs';

            const body = [
              '## Bundle Size Report',
              '',
              '| Directory | Size |',
              '|-----------|------|',
              `| \`.next/static\` | ${staticSize} |`,
              `| \`.next/server\` | ${serverSize} |`,
              `| **Total \`.next\`** | **${totalSize}** |`,
              '',
              `**Per-route gzip budget:** ${budgetOutcome}`,
              '',
              `> Measured at commit ${context.sha.substring(0, 7)}`,
            ].join('\n');

            // Find existing comment to update
            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const marker = '## Bundle Size Report';
            const existing = comments.find(c => c.body.startsWith(marker));

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

name: License Compliance

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [develop, main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  license-check:
    name: License Compliance Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # Production deps: enforced as a true allowlist (permissive-only + documented
      # exceptions), not a denylist. `license-checker --onlyAllow` matches by substring
      # (e.g. an allowed "MIT" token also silently matches "FSL-1.1-MIT"), so it cannot
      # actually enforce this policy — see scripts/check-production-licenses.ts for the
      # exact-SPDX-token matching this uses instead, and docs/project/license-exceptions.md
      # for the exception list. (#847 / SE-M3)
      - name: Check production licenses (blocking allowlist)
        run: npm run check-licenses

      # Dev/build deps: scan the full tree and report strong-copyleft findings.
      # Build-time-only tooling (e.g. lightningcss MPL-2.0) never ships to clients,
      # so this step is non-blocking — it surfaces dev-dep licenses for review.
      # See docs/project/license-exceptions.md → "Dev-dependency scanning". (#623)
      - name: Report dev-dependency licenses (non-blocking)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          echo "::group::Dev + production license summary"
          npx license-checker --summary
          echo "::endgroup::"
          echo "Scanning full dependency tree (incl. devDependencies) for strong copyleft..."
          npx license-checker --failOn "GPL-2.0;GPL-3.0;AGPL-1.0;AGPL-3.0;SSPL-1.0;BSL-1.1;CPAL-1.0;OSL-3.0;CPOL-1.02" \
            || echo "::warning::Strong-copyleft license found in dev/build dependencies — review docs/project/license-exceptions.md"

name: Security Scan

on:
  push:
    branches: [develop, main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [develop, main]
  schedule:
    # Run daily at 8:00 UTC (was weekly — CVE detection latency reduced from ~6 days to <24h)
    - cron: '0 8 * * *'

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  develop_push_source:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      checks: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/validate-merged-pr.yml
    with:
      required_checks: '["Gitleaks secret scan","npm audit","Vercel env safety"]'

  gitleaks:
    name: Gitleaks secret scan
    needs: develop_push_source
    if: always() && needs.develop_push_source.outputs.validated_by_pr != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install Gitleaks
        run: |
          GITLEAKS_VERSION="8.21.2"
          wget -q "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}/gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_linux_x64.tar.gz"
          tar xzf "gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_linux_x64.tar.gz"
          chmod +x gitleaks

      - name: Run Gitleaks
        run: ./gitleaks detect --source . --verbose

  audit:
    name: npm audit
    needs: develop_push_source
    if: always() && needs.develop_push_source.outputs.validated_by_pr != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run security audit (production deps)
        # Audit production dependencies only (dev vulns don't affect the deployed
        # application). Threshold is "moderate" so medium-severity issues are caught
        # before they accumulate into high/critical ones.
        run: npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate

      - name: Report all vulnerabilities (informational)
        if: always()
        run: npm audit || true

  vercel-env-safety:
    name: Vercel env safety
    needs: develop_push_source
    if: always() && needs.develop_push_source.outputs.validated_by_pr != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    env:
      VERCEL_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
      VERCEL_PROJECT_ID: ${{ vars.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }}
      VERCEL_ORG_ID: ${{ vars.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
      SECRETS_WITHHELD_PR: >-
        ${{
          github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
          (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork == true ||
           github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')
        }}

    steps:
      # `.vercel/project.json` is gitignored, so project/org IDs must come
      # from repository variables instead of a checked-in metadata file.
      # Configure `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` and `VERCEL_ORG_ID` under
      # Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables.
      #
      # VERCEL_TOKEN (a secret) is REQUIRED for this job to do anything.
      # DO-M2 (#829): it has never been set, so this job used to skip its one
      # assertion step and still report success on every push/schedule run —
      # "requiredness without evidence," the same pattern this project
      # rejected for Dependabot preview smoke tests (see the Dependabot
      # branch in preview-smoke.yml). Skip-to-pass is reserved for fork and
      # Dependabot PRs, where GitHub genuinely withholds secrets (expected
      # sandboxing, not a gap). On push, schedule, and ordinary same-repo PR
      # runs, a missing token fails the job loudly instead of silently passing.
      #
      # ACTION REQUIRED (human, repo admin): add VERCEL_TOKEN under
      # Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Secrets. Until that is
      # done, this job is EXPECTED to fail on every push/schedule run — that
      # is the fix working as intended, not a regression.
      - name: Fail when Vercel credentials are unavailable (trusted event)
        if: >-
          ${{
            (env.VERCEL_TOKEN == '' || env.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID == '' || env.VERCEL_ORG_ID == '') &&
            env.SECRETS_WITHHELD_PR != 'true'
          }}
        run: |
          echo "::error::Vercel env safety check cannot run: VERCEL_TOKEN (secret) plus VERCEL_PROJECT_ID and VERCEL_ORG_ID (repo variables) are required."
          echo "::error::VERCEL_TOKEN is missing. A human with repo admin access must add it under Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Secrets before this job can pass again."
          echo "::error::This is the only automated check on deployed Vercel environment state in this repo (DO-M2 / issue #829) — it must fail rather than silently report success while checking nothing."
          exit 1

      - name: Skip when Vercel credentials are unavailable (secret-withheld PR)
        if: >-
          ${{
            (env.VERCEL_TOKEN == '' || env.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID == '' || env.VERCEL_ORG_ID == '') &&
            env.SECRETS_WITHHELD_PR == 'true'
          }}
        run: |
          echo "GitHub withholds repository secrets from fork and Dependabot PR workflow runs."
          echo "Skipping the Vercel env safety assertion in this secret-withheld PR context."

      - name: Assert legacy agent override is absent from Vercel env
        if: ${{ env.VERCEL_TOKEN != '' && env.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID != '' && env.VERCEL_ORG_ID != '' }}
        run: |
          legacy_key="$(printf '%s_%s_%s\n' ALLOW AGENT RUN)"
          response="$(curl -fsS \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN" \
            "https://api.vercel.com/v10/projects/$VERCEL_PROJECT_ID/env?teamId=$VERCEL_ORG_ID&limit=100")"

          echo "$response" | jq -r '.envs[]?.key' > env-keys.txt

          if grep -Fxq "$legacy_key" env-keys.txt; then
            echo "::error::Legacy agent runner override is still configured in Vercel. Remove it before deploy."
            exit 1
          fi
